subject: Cloud Computing
title: The GPU Cloud Wars
description: A 60-second lesson on The GPU Cloud Wars.

hook.text: NVIDIA H100 GPUs cost $30,000 each and sell out instantly. Cloud providers are in an arms race to stockpile them.

buildup.text: Every major AI company needs GPU clusters. Providers, startups, and governments all compete for limited supply.

discovery.text: New GPU cloud startups (CoreWeave, Lambda Labs) offer pure GPU compute without the complexity of traditional cloud.

twist.text: Custom AI chips are emerging: Google TPUs, AWS Trainium, and Microsoft's Maia. The GPU monopoly may not last forever.

climax.text: The GPU shortage is reshaping cloud economics. AI compute is the new premium resource, like storage was in the 2000s.

punchline.text: GPUs are the new gold. Cloud providers fight for every chip.

quiz.question: How are cloud providers responding to the GPU shortage?
options: By developing custom AI chips to reduce dependence on NVIDIA GPUs
By stopping all AI services until more GPUs are available
By sharing their GPU inventory with competing cloud providers

details.summary: Cloud providers are competing fiercely for GPU capacity as AI demand skyrockets. NVIDIA GPU availability has become a strategic bottleneck, driving providers to secure supply, build custom AI chips, and offer increasingly specialized GPU instance types.
details.whyItMatters: GPU availability determines who can build and serve AI models. The GPU cloud wars shape which providers lead the AI era and affect pricing for every organization using cloud AI infrastructure.
takeaways: NVIDIA GPU demand far exceeds current supply
Providers build custom chips to reduce NVIDIA dependency
GPU instance availability varies significantly by provider and region

faq.question: Why are GPUs so scarce in the cloud?
faq.answer: AI model training and inference require massive GPU clusters. Demand from AI companies, enterprises adopting AI, and cloud providers building their own AI services far exceeds NVIDIA's manufacturing capacity. Wait times for cloud GPU instances can extend weeks to months.

faq.question: What custom AI chips are cloud providers building?
faq.answer: Google has TPUs now in their sixth generation. AWS offers Trainium for training and Inferentia for inference. Microsoft is developing Maia for AI and Cobalt for general compute. These custom chips reduce dependence on NVIDIA and provide cost-effective alternatives.
